diagram_name: Anatomy of a GitHub Repository Page
chapter_title: Open File Formats and Version Control
learning_objective: The learner will identify the eight parts of a repository page that a reviewer reads, from a description of each part's appearance, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** github-repository-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the eight parts of a repository page that a reviewer reads, from a description of each part's appearance, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** GitHub Repository, Version Control, Git (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The README is the license. (2) The fork button changes the original repository. (3) The file list shows only the final version. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a page is a Remember-level task, and an illustration of the page places each part where the reviewer will find it. The quiz asks the learner to go from the look of a part to its name, which is how they will navigate a real repository. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of a repository page in a browser frame. Under the page header is a row of five small tabs. At the upper right is a small button with a branching-line icon. At the left, above the main area, is a drop-down box. Below it is a thin strip holding a small round avatar and one short line of text, and beside the strip is a small clock icon with a number. Under the strip is a column of rows, each with a folder icon or a file icon. Below the column is a large block of text lines. In a narrow column at the right is a small scales icon beside a short line. The eight markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Tab row | A row of five small tabs under the page header. | The tabs switch between the files, the reported problems (issues), and the proposed changes (pull requests). | Open the issues tab to see problems others have found. | | 2 | Fork button | A small button with a branching-line icon at the upper right. | Creates your own copy of the repository, which you can change without touching the original. | Fork before you revise, so the original stays as the author left it. | | 3 | Branch selector | A drop-down box at the left above the main area. | Switches between lines of work, like the main line and a branch for a new feature. | The main branch is the usual place to read the current version. | | 4 | Latest commit strip | A thin strip with a small round avatar and one short line of text. | Shows who made the most recent change, what they said about it, and when. | A last commit that is years old suggests the resource is no longer maintained. | | 5 | Commit history link | A small clock icon with a number beside it. | Opens the full list of commits, with authors, dates, and messages. | Use it to date your evidence: cite the commit you reviewed. | | 6 | File list | A column of rows, each with a folder icon or a file icon. | Lists the source files and folders in the repository. | Check the file types: Markdown or HTML suggest an editable source. | | 7 | README | A large block of text lines below the file list. | Explains what the resource is, how its files fit together, and how to use it. | A README is the note that the editable source metric's seventh check asks for. | | 8 | License entry | A small scales icon beside a short line in the narrow column at the right. | Shows the repository's license, taken from its license file. | Compare it with the license statement on the resource itself. | **Provenance:** The parts follow the chapter section "GitHub Repository". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the page "illustrative example". The sim states that the layout of a real GitHub page can change over time and that the parts, not their positions, are what a reviewer should look for. **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 8 in the order of the table. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 8 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can read a repository page." Below 7 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with eight numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists the parts of a repository page as the file list, the README, the license file, the commit history, issues, and pull requests. The chapter says a README is the short note that explains how the pieces fit together.
